page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 248.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.75 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific workloads. The server achieves a static web serving throughput of 51.15 GB/sec and shows strong performance in Geekbench image processing (15287.0) and text processing (2637.0). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 144.63 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 61.79 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 support facilitate strong LLM inference speeds on small models, reaching 421.19 tokens/sec for text generation with a 135M model. However, performance drops significantly on larger models, with 70B model text generation falling to a poor tier of 2.38 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-32 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive workloads without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation and large L3 cache make it appropriate for database operations, software compilation, memory-cached web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
